actual_scope: The P104 decoder wall in the row model (each rank-1 decoder term is one owned chain priced by its climb): (1) the row price, climb >= F2 rank of the label pairing over the (deposit, gather) supports, and the exact 8-row x 7 = 56 E8 decoder with rank-8 rigidity; (2) partial replacement of 4 of the 8 rows: <= 3 rows impossible, exactly 4 rows cost >= 28 (all 70 R), exactly 5 rows cost >= 28 (both R orbits; finite check by a C++ enumerator, pinned summary plus an independent stdlib spot-check); (3) the cross-pair identity and the half-integer partial-replacement bound |R|(8-|R|), the graded 2-adic rank bound, the rank-certificate lemma and C >= n/2 for distinct labels of F2-rank <= 6, and the proof that functional-split certificates cannot reach h = 9; (4) open: >= 6 replacement rows, the h = 9 wall, and the conjectured junk trade-off C >= 104 - 48J/4,992.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a constructive helper-basis or causal-split improvement. This package collects lower bounds on the owned decoder mass of P104 (the 56 owned units per plane that every P104 word pays), so others can see which decoder changes are ruled out and which remain open; it makes no kappa claim and ships no new word.
bottleneck_link: The decoder's 56 owned units per plane are a fixed part of every P104 invoice; one unit less is worth about +2.4% kappa per plane (our price model, not re-checked here). These bounds show which decoder redesigns cannot pay and where the remaining room is.
stop_rule: Every proved claim has a proof in PROOF.md and every finite fact a standard-library exact checker (or, for the five-row enumeration, a pinned summary plus an independent check); open items stated as open; validator PASS.
evidence: README.md, PROOF.md, rows.py, partial.py, fiverow.py, halfwall.py, lane/ (C++ enumerator source), VERIFY.json.

open_questions.question: Do k >= 6 rank-1 rows replacing 4 E8 rows of P104 always cost >= 28?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the last partial-replacement case for 4 rows; a sub-28 design would be the first owned saving on the P104 decoder.
open_questions.first_step: Prove the union-rigidity lemma (README section 4) on the 252 dangerous cheap-row profiles, keeping each closure's subspace structure.

open_questions.question: Is C >= n/2 true for every set of distinct labels of F2-rank 9 (in particular C >= 52 on P104 labels)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would bound every decoder redesign on 9-bit labels at 52 owned units per plane, i.e. at most 4 units below E8.
open_questions.first_step: Look for non-split certificates Z of rank <= 18 on the full flag that stay below 2 x climb on smaller flags (functional splits are ruled out).

open_questions.question: Does every decoder on P104 labels satisfy C >= 104 - 48 J/4,992, J = nonzero junk cells?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would say trading owned mass for junk is never better than the chord between E8 (56, 4,992) and M = I (104, 0).
open_questions.first_step: Combine the certificate lemma with a junk-weighted Z (zero on kept junk cells) and test it on the block designs.
